> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **32** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json abb6df0e0109f32c8a51f94a4deaaa4518a0b5a2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `64be5534158d34414352b7d2414f09fc48449831` — the merge of head `90e7060f9dd80e4a8c8aaea772ac3da487b3f07f` into base `abb6df0e0109f32c8a51f94a4deaaa4518a0b5a2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 64be5534158d34414352b7d2414f09fc48449831 && git checkout 64be5534158d34414352b7d2414f09fc48449831
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin abb6df0e0109f32c8a51f94a4deaaa4518a0b5a2 90e7060f9dd80e4a8c8aaea772ac3da487b3f07f && git checkout -B drift-repro abb6df0e0109f32c8a51f94a4deaaa4518a0b5a2 && git merge --no-ff 90e7060f9dd80e4a8c8aaea772ac3da487b3f07f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json abb6df0e0109f32c8a51f94a4deaaa4518a0b5a2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs abb6df0e0109f32c8a51f94a4deaaa4518a0b5a2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `90e7060f9dd80e4a8c8aaea772ac3da487b3f07f`
Local-runs: none

Scope: owed by the `Clause-②: yes` declaration alone (no `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed path, no `(narrowing)` declaration on this PR's committed tree). Read: the PR's diff at this head, card #23848 and its claim `6213346689`, and the head's check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **A Turso REMOTE primary is accepted by `os migrate plan` and `os migrate apply`.** Before: both refused at the boot (`Deferred schema DDL is not supported by the Turso REMOTE transport`). After: both boot with `deferredDdlUnsupported: 'skip-schema-sync'`, the posture `os migrate organization-ownership` already uses, and still pass identical boot options, as `apply.ts`'s own comment requires. This is the widening the declaration names, and it is correct: the remedy the platform prints for destructive drift (`os migrate apply --allow-destructive`) could not run on that transport at all.
2. **The additive half on that boot is reported as not examined, never as none.** Human output: `SKIPPED_SCHEMA_SYNC_NOTE` under the database line, plus PARTIAL wording on a drift-free result. `--json`: `schemaSync: 'skipped'`; an apply with no drift answers `in_sync_partial`, not `in_sync`. Correct: an empty `pending` from a boot that examined nothing would otherwise read as "every declared table exists".
3. **`notApplied` (new `--json` field) and a PARTIAL verdict.** `skipped` keeps both kinds; `notApplied` is `skipped` minus the entries held back for lack of `--allow-destructive` (`deferred`, by reference). A confirmed destructive entry the driver did not apply answers `message: 'partial'`, exit `1`; a non-destructive one is named and exits `0`. The field is additive. The exit change applies on every dialect, and only on a path where a confirmed destructive change was not performed: a run that used to exit `0` with a count now exits `1`. That narrows the success exit toward the truth ("absence must be loud"), and the changeset states it in its own paragraph. No published schema carries this document.
4. **Published surface.** `@objectstack/cli`: `SKIPPED_SCHEMA_SYNC_NOTE` is a new export of `src/utils/schema-migrate.ts`, which none of the package's entries (`.`, `./console`, `./hook-body`) re-exports, so it is not a published symbol. `@objectstack/driver-turso`: entry `.` only; the diff changes the text of `REMOTE_DRIFT_REPORT_CAVEAT` (the value of `driftReportCaveat`) and one docblock, no signature. The caveat's one reader, `runArtifactBootMigrationGate`, branches on its presence and prints it, so the gate's behaviour (warn and boot on remote) is unchanged.
5. **The caveat text is true after both PRs.** On this head it keeps #23847 / PR #23893's NOT NULL sentences byte-for-byte as `origin/main` has them, and replaces only the clause this card made false ("a destructive entry has no remedy … `os migrate apply` refuses against it"). The gate comment in `artifact-boot-migration.ts` states the same two facts.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes` takes at least `minor`. The changeset declares `@objectstack/cli: minor` and `@objectstack/driver-turso: minor`, carries the line-initial `Clause-②: yes`, and names the accepted input, the new `notApplied` field, `schemaSync` / `in_sync_partial`, and the exit-code change on other dialects. Consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The dev's `open_questions`: none.
- `packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migrate.ts` was "read, not edited unless measured necessary" on the claim; it was edited because its `deferredDdlUnsupported` docblock became false and to host the one shared sentence. Accepted: necessary, internal, and stated in the report and PR.
- The remote-face pins skip in CI (no `sqld` on the runners); the measurement of record is the dev's local run against a real `sqld`, cited in the PR body. Not a contract flag, but a reader of this record should know the CI green does not include the remote face.
- Out of scope, filed: #23925 (the plan prints `--allow-destructive` as the remedy for an entry the remote face cannot apply).

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-23848-migrate-apply-turso-remote`
Reviewed-by: `session_01PFB9ZGRWYvjhTXsd8i6KBp`

**VERDICT: PASS**
